scientific_name: Strobilanthes kunthiana (Nees) T. Anderson ex Benth.
accepted_name: Strobilanthes kunthiana (Nees) T. Anderson ex Benth.
native_region: Endemic to shola-grassland ecosystems of the Southern Western Ghats in South India
habitat: High-altitude shola-grassland slopes above 1,800 meters elevation
ecological_importance: Synchronous mass flowering triggers massive population surges in pollinators, bees, and birds.
threats: Conversion of native shola-grasslands to exotic tree plantations
field_identification_notes: Hairy elliptic leaves with prominent venation found in high-elevation grassland ecosystems.
Striking purplish-blue bell-shaped flowers appearing en masse during synchronous 12-year bloom cycles.
Woody shrub stems drying after seeding.
ml_relevance: Purplish-blue bell-shaped flowers during bloom phase and pubescent elliptic leaves.

ar_information.quick_identification: Hairy elliptic leaves; vibrant purplish-blue bell flowers.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Keystone species driving multi-year pollinator booms.
ar_information.conservation_message: Endangered (EN) due to restricted habitat. Famous for its mass gregarious flowering spectacle occurring precisely once every 12 years, turning hill slopes completely blue.
